lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: Hello.

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: This should be my last request.

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: Proceed to the coordinates I've sent,

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: and confirm if the bottle is empty or not.
How are you sure there will be a bottle there?

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: I met with some of my father's old friends.

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: They said he took a bottle of booze with him everywhere he went.

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: The drink names match as well.

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: So it should be there.

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: ... That place is also where my father died.
Is that everything you can tell me?

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: Would telling you more be helpful?
Of course.

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: Hmm...
Chilipepper doesn't say anything for a long time.

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: Constructing the Outpost

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: was a herculean effort. Time-consuming and complicated.

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: Whenever he wasn't working, my father's routine consisted entirely of getting drunk and sleeping.

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: He never gave me so much as a second glance.

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: I had to endure that for 10 long years, and I resented him for it.

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: One day, I couldn't take it anymore,

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: and I screamed that if he dropped dead, I wouldn't shed a tear.

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: If anything, I'd end up vomiting

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: because his corpse would reek of booze.

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: Something along those lines.

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: I left home and cut all ties with my father.

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: I never considered that those drinks he had after work

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: were his one and only solace.

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: A few years later, when construction was nearly finished,

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: I understood my father more than I did before.

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: I couldn't bring myself to apologize to his face,

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: so I bought him a set of whiskey.

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: I figured if he was willing to drink all of it, and bring back the empty bottle,

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: it would in some way show that he'd forgiven me.

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: I wanted to join him, but I can't drink.

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: One day, he went up to gather materials

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: and never returned.

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: Eventually, I saw his name on a list of casualties.

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: Sigh...

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: So that's my story.

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: I just hope, at the very end...

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: that my father was able to forgive me.

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: Not that we'll ever find anything.
I'm sure we will.

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: That would be the best.

lines.speaker: chilipepper
lines.text: I'll wait for an update from you.
